Note::TexAccessor::subsections¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::subsections() const

Extract Subsection Titles Per Source Cell¶

subsections() extracts the required brace body from each complete \subsection or \subsection* command. It is useful when a document’s subsection structure must be listed or indexed independently of the body text between headings.

An optional square-bracket short-title argument is accepted but not returned: in \subsection[Short]{Nested {title}}, the token is the full brace body, Nested {title}, not the abbreviated Short form — unlike captions, whose required body must be non-nested, a subsection title’s brace body may itself contain a balanced nested group, and that nested group is retained verbatim in the token.

The extractor is lexical and command-exact: \subsection and \subsection* are matched, but the longer, unrelated command name \subsectional{...} in the same source is not (it is not a \subsection invocation at all — the match requires the control word to end exactly at subsection or subsection*), and an incomplete call such as \subsection{broken with no closing brace produces no token. A deeper heading, \subsubsection{...}, is a different command and is not matched — see subsubsections for that level.

The closed TokenBatch stores every extracted title in its rank-1 Text tokens() Note. Its Int64 offsets() has source.numel() + 1 entries, so flattened source cell i owns [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). The original rank and shape determine lane order but are not imposed on a ragged token count. The receiver is not mutated.

Undefined yields undefined tokens with offsets [0]. Empty cells, malformed commands, and cells without subsections produce empty intervals. Only Text is accepted. Extraction scans source bytes and allocates the captured titles and one offset per source cell.

Example 1: Optional Argument, Nested Body, Escaped, Unrelated, And Broken Calls¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\subsection[Short]{Nested {title}} \subsection*{Second})",
    R"(\\subsection{escaped} \subsectional{long} \subsection{broken)",
    R"(\subsubsection{deeper} \subsection{Third})"});
const auto subsections = source.tex().subsections();

std::cout << subsections.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Nested {title}", "Second", "Third"]

The optional Short value is discarded and the nested {title} group is kept whole. The second cell contributes nothing: the escaped \\subsection, the unrelated \subsectional, and the unterminated \subsection{broken all fail to match. The third cell’s \subsubsection{deeper} is a different command and is skipped; only its trailing \subsection{Third} matches.

Example 2: Per-Cell Offsets¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = subsections.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 2, 3]

Cell 0 owns two titles, cell 1 owns none, and cell 2 owns exactly the one title that matched.

Example 3: A 2-D Grid, Ragged Ownership Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\subsection{A})", "plain",
                             R"(\subsection{B}\subsection{C})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto grid_batch = grid.tex().subsections();
std::cout << grid_batch.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A", "B", "C"]

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().subsections().tokens().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().subsections();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "subsections Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
subsections Int64: rejected
